title: BoltzGen designs a miniprotein that blocks MAP7 binding to kinesin-1
summary: Starting from an AlphaFold3 model of the kinesin-1 coiled-coil stalk, BoltzGen was used to design Sidetrak, a 36-amino-acid miniprotein binding kinesin-1 with nanomolar affinity. Binding required the TPR docking site and was abolished by interface mutation. Sidetrak inhibited MAP7 binding, reduced MAP7-dependent kinesin-1 recruitment to microtubules in cells and redistributed mitochondria toward the nucleus, with selective association with kinesin-1 complexes by interaction proteomics. Only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: BoltzGen de novo miniprotein design from an AlphaFold3 structural model

evidence.tested: Binding assays, interface mutants, cell experiments and interaction proteomics.
evidence.unknown: Exact affinity and design success rate, not given in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: BoltzGen generated the miniprotein binder from the AlphaFold3 model.
